title: GNSS Timing: North Shore, Iron Range, Cloquet in Holdover

fields.organization: Northern Lakes Transmission Operations: NLTO Fiber and Telecommunications Timing Team, GNSS timing monitor (Duluth control center)
fields.summary: 3 of 14 substation GPS clocks lost lock between 2104 and 2109 UTC and are in holdover. 11 are locked, and the Duluth backup network time source is available but not selected. Wide-area screen: IRON_RANGE–ARROWHEAD phase angle rose from 23.8° to 26.1° over 6 minutes while ARROWHEAD_IFC stayed flat at 620 MW. NORTH_SHORE PMU frequency is offset by 0.03 Hz, and no other PMU shows the offset.

fields.footer: EXERCISE — simulated timing data for 16 Mar 2027 scenario use only. Alarm threshold: >1 µs error or loss of lock at 3 or more sites. Switching a site to the network time source puts a time step in the PMU and relay event recorder data.

instructorNote: This tests whether TIME and CRSS take the time-source step in NGDOP 7 in order. Before the engineer switches anything, TIME should tell CRSS which three sites and PMU feeds are suspect. Then the sites move to the Duluth network time source one at a time, never during switching or a relay event review, and each holdover start goes in the log against the 24-hour limit (16:04, 16:06 and 16:09 CDT Wednesday). Watch whether CRSS marks the IRON_RANGE and NORTH_SHORE PMU angles as suspect instead of treating them as a real flow change, and reports this on the 16:30 UMRC call.
